questions.question: / [CO1]Explain the biochemical pathway of ethanol metabolism, naming the enzymes involved and the intermediate products formed. Why is acetaldehyde considered toxic?
questions.solution_html:
• Explain the biochemical pathway of ethanol metabolism, naming the enzymes involved
  • and the intermediate products formed. Why is acetaldehyde considered toxic?
  • • In ethanol metabolism, human body breaks down and eliminates alcohol. The final
  • products are carbon dioxide and water.
  • • The breakdown takes place in the liver.
  • • In the first step, ethanol is oxidized to acetaldehyde in the presence of the enzyme
  • Alcohol Dehydrogenase
  • CH3CH2OH CH3CHO NADH HNAD
  • • Acetaldehyde is oxidized into acetate in the presence of the enzyme Aldehyde
  • Dehydrogenase
  • • Acetic acid coenzyme A ligase (ACSL) breaks down acetic acid into acetyl-CoA,
  • which is then broken down into carbon dioxide and water
  • Acetaldehyde is toxic because it rapidly binds to proteins and DNA, causes oxidative
  • stress, and contributes to hangovers and liver damage
  • (Metabolism 4 marks+ toxicity of acetic acid 1 mark)
questions.source_exam: MGU-UGP (HONOURS) 2024 Admission Regular Exam Sem 4, March 2026
